name: Drought
value: Sudan harvest hit; no famine declared
summary: El Niño drought cuts Sudan's harvest and raises famine risk; no new famine declaration or exporter harvest failure found
state: Sudan's July–September rains were the lowest in more than three decades, with North Darfur's the lowest since 1984, and an IPC alert on 12 Oct warned that famine risk is growing in conflict-affected areas (Reuters via Arab News, 23 Oct). Some farmers expect about a quarter of last year's yield, while WFP has less than half of last year's Sudan budget and has cut rations. Severe drought in a major crop region keeps this at Watch; searches on 15 Nov found no new drought-driven famine declaration or major exporter harvest failure.
for_you: The worst effects fall on farming and displaced households in Sudan, where poor harvests tend to push up local food prices and aid needs over the following months. Global grain supply is not directly affected.
rubric_hit: Watch: severe drought in a major crop region (Sudan, lowest rains in 30+ years); no famine declaration or exporter harvest failure

sources.title: Arab News (Reuters) — New famine risk haunts war-torn Sudan with El Niño-driven drought

why: Drought slowly destroys harvests, hydropower and river shipping, and drives famine and migration.
drivers: Rainfall deficits, heat, ENSO, groundwater depletion.

rubric.alert: Drought driving famine conditions, a major exporter's harvest failure, or monsoon failure across a major breadbasket.
rubric.watch: Severe drought in a major crop region, a major river at record low, or a monsoon running more than 20% below normal.
rubric.normal: No major breadbasket in severe drought.
